name: Northwest Pipeline Parachute Lateral Expansion

values.StartLocation: Parachute gas processing plant area, Garfield County

researcher_notes: Not an existing row: the roster holds Northwest Gas Pipeline P0230 as the system plus named project rows (Trail West, Kalama Lateral, Kelso-Beaver, Wild Trail), none for this lateral. The Colorado Interstate Gas Parachute Lateral is a different pipe. Completed lateral of 38 miles (about 61 km), over the 25 km new-pipe threshold, so it is shaped as a project row under the parent name. The EIA August 2026 table (Historical Projects sheet, Excel row 447, FERC docket CP06-45) lists 38 miles, 30 inches, 450 million cubic feet per day, completed 15 May 2007. The Northwest Pipeline annual report for 2006 (filed with the SEC) says the company applied in January 2006 for a 38-mile, 30-inch lateral from the Parachute area to the Greasewood area in northwest Colorado, with new capacity of 450 thousand dekatherms per day, and that FERC granted the certificate in August 2006. The annual report for 2007 says the lateral entered service on 16 May 2007 and that ownership moved to Parachute Pipeline LLC, owned by a Williams affiliate, on 31 December 2007. Owner is therefore staged as Parachute Pipeline LLC; the entity was not found in the owner gazetteer and no legal-form check beyond the name was done. Parent not staged because the owner tab link to Williams was not checked against the gazetteer. A FERC notice puts the length at about 37.6 miles; 38 is used as both main sources state it. Cost left blank on purpose: EIA states 57.8 million dollars while the 2006 annual report estimated 86 million dollars before construction, and the two do not agree. Current operating status after 2007 was not independently checked. No route found, so route is left as no route; check the FERC filings for alignment maps. Tier high: EIA and the SEC filings are separate origins.
